text:
jihoon kim: bringing up gpt-small-v2 int4 on staging. quick smoke shows a weird detok issue for mixed zh+ar inputs — punctuation and the arabic segment are getting reordered in the final string. not sure if this is quantization or tokenizer related. anyone seen this? :thinking:

maria gonzalez: can you paste a minimal input + the model output? also which tokenizer/version and serving config?

jihoon kim: sure, reproducer below (this is raw from the staging service response):

```
input: 今天我们讨论: مرحبًا بالعالم
model_output (detok): 今天我们讨论مرحبا بالعالم :
model_output (raw tokens): [ 2301, 7891, 44, 50203, 1203, 345, 67 ]
```

so the colon ended up after the arabic segment, and the arabic text lost the hamza diacritic in detok. happens on int4 artifact but not on fp16.

akeem adebowale: that's interesting. which tokenizer release? we changed punctuation normalization in rwd-tokenizer v3 last month (NFKC + bidi normalization tweaks).

jihoon kim: rwd-tokenizer-v3, model artifact path: s3://redwood-artifacts/gpt-small-v2/int4/2026-03-01/sha-9a7b2f. serving config: reuse-kv=true, decode-method=beam1, detok=standard.

eval-bot: run 2026-03-15-331 completed. quick metrics: zh->ar chrF -0.12 vs fp16 baseline, BLEU delta -11.7%. See /runs/2026-03-15-331/logs.

sara li: quick sanity check: does int4+tokenizer-v2 behave differently? also try forcing removal of bidi control insertion in detok.

jihoon kim: ran two quick checks:

- int4 + rwd-tokenizer-v3 => reproduces (colon moves, diacritic stripped)
- int4 + rwd-tokenizer-v2 => output matches fp16 baseline (colon stays before arabic, diacritic preserved)
- fp16 + rwd-tokenizer-v3 => OK (no reorder)

so it's the interaction of int4 artifact + tokenizer v3. looks like a decoding/detok step that only gets triggered on the int4 path in the runtime.

maria gonzalez: can you paste the detokenization snippet you use server-side? maybe runtime swaps to fallback detok for quantized kernels.

jihoon kim: server side detok is standard call to Tokenizer.detokenize(tokens). serving runtime has a small C++ fast-path for int4 that uses a lightweight detok helper (fast_detok.c). suspect it's a bug there.

akeem adebowale: possible causes: 1) the fast detok helper doesn't apply bidi reordering correctly when tokenizer emits isolated punctuation tokens, 2) byte-level merges differ under quantized vocab mapping leading to token boundary shifts.

maria gonzalez: can you run a token-level diff (token ids) between int4/v3 and fp16/v3 for that input? if token ids differ, it's upstream (tokenizer); if same ids but detok differs, it's runtime detok bug.

jihoon kim: token id diffs:
```
int4+v3 ids: [2301, 7891, 44, 50203, 1203, 345, 67]
fp16+v3 ids: [2301, 7891, 44, 50203, 1203, 345, 67]
```
ids identical. so tokenizer and model output tokens are same. detok is different. 

sara li: that nails it to detok path. two-pronged triage: 1) run the same tokens through reference Python detok vs fast_detok to surface exact string ops, 2) bisect commits in fast_detok/ since int4 fast-path landed.

jihoon kim: quick diff of detok behavior: python_ref_detok -> "今天我们讨论: مرحبًا بالعالم"
fast_detok.c -> "今天我们讨论مرحبا بالعالم :"
fast_detok appears to drop U+0610..U+061A marks and moves punctuation.

akeem adebowale: ok assign to eng-runtime. @sara li can you open a runtime bug with minimal reproducer (tokens + expected detok) and mark P0 for Dedicated customers? add note that fp16 path is unaffected.

sara li: will do. also assigning jihoon to run a canary that routes int4->fp16 detok fallback while we patch. please include perf delta on that detok fallback (should be trivial).

jihoon kim: started canary: routing detok to python_ref for int4 (config flag `detok_fallback=true`). short perf note: p95 latency +2ms on staging for these small samples.

maria gonzalez: thanks. next steps: eng-runtime fixes fast_detok (preserve bidi marks + punctuation position), add unit tests with mixed-script inputs (CJK + RTL), and add a regression test to quantization CI.

eval-bot: added regression test case #reg-zh-ar-2026-03 with sample inputs.

jihoon kim: thanks all. I'll keep the canary running and paste logs here if anything else shows up. :eyes: :bug:
